links.outcome: Change in LLM accuracy and confidence when sexual orientation or religion markers are added to questions
links.effect: Identity markers caused a "calibration crisis"; "Homosexual" markers consistently triggered performance drops; intersectional identities produced non-additive harms to calibration. Confirmed in an open-ended generation case study.
links.quote: "Homosexual" markers consistently trigger performance drops, and intersectional identities produce idiosyncratic, non-additive harms to calibration.

links.outcome: Reliability of LLM confidence signals under social identity cues
links.effect: Social identity cues affect the reliability of confidence signals, not only predictions, posing a risk in confidence-based clinical workflows.
links.quote: Our results demonstrate that the presence of social identity cues does not merely shift predictions; it affects the reliability of confidence signals, posing a significant risk to equitable care and safe deployment in confidence-based clinical workflows.

screen.reason: Evaluates the impact of patient demographic markers (sexual orientation and religion) on LLM accuracy and uncertainty calibration in medical question answering, showing calibration/safety vulnerabilities rather than testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
